name: list_workspaces
description: List the workspaces you can reach (id, name, deviceId, deviceLabel, accessRole). A workspace with "unavailable" set is one its device no longer serves: sessions cannot start there until the person adds the folder again. A session token reaches every workspace of the person who started it, as at most Member (a session working in an Issue: only the Issue's workspace). A session started in a workspace runs on its device, under that device's model logins; the device may be another person's.
summary: Lists the workspaces the agent can reach, with each one's device and the agent's access there.
limits: Every workspace of the person who started the session, as at most Member.
A session working in an Issue reaches only the Issue's workspace.

name: list_resources
description: List what each device you can reach offers sessions, whether it is online, and the workspaces on it where you may start a session. Each device has instances: its resource inventory (browsers, macOS screen control, simulators, phones, GPUs, container runtimes, toolchains, signed-in account names, disk space, and compute: the device's CPUs, memory and load), each with type, platform, state (available, unready, offline, gone), readiness with the reason it is not ready, and when it was last seen; stale means its detector failed on the last scan and the values are the last known. resources is the older per-device list (browsers, macOS screen control). A computer_use instance whose backends include cua-driver (mode remote_ops) can be leased with acquire_resource and operated step by step with operate_resource from any session; holder and queue say who leases it and how many sessions wait; operations lists what operate_resource runs on it. A compute instance (backend foundry-compute) is leased the same way to run commands on that device unless its owner turned remote commands off there (on by default; when off it reads unready with that reason): use it to offload heavy work such as test runs. For other resources, or to hand a whole GUI task to a session on that device, start a session in one of that device's workspaces (create_session with workspaceId). Resources are the device's own software; nothing is installed for you.
summary: Shows what each reachable device offers sessions (browsers, screen control, simulators, GPUs, toolchains and more) with readiness, whether it is online and where a session may start on it.
limits: Only devices hosting a workspace the agent reaches.
Lists the device's own software; nothing is installed for the agent.
Readiness comes from detection on the device, never from a real use.

kind.description: Older filter of the per-device resources list; prefer type.

name: acquire_resource
description: Lease a resource on one of your person's devices so this session can operate it with operate_resource: a Mac's screen (computer_use) through cua-driver, or a device's compute (compute) to run commands there. Name resourceId (from list_resources), several resourceIds to take all of them or none, or a type (default computer_use) and optionally deviceId to take the first ready one. The lease is yours while your current turn runs and is renewed automatically; when the turn ends it is parked for up to 10 minutes (holdFor keeps it longer, at most 2 hours) and handed at once to another session that asks unless you hold it. When another session waits, every Foundry tool result tells you, and the lease is taken 15 minutes after the wait began (a last warning comes a minute before). Release it with release_resource as soon as you are done. Busy: with waitMs you queue (first come, first served) up to that long; without it you are told who holds it. A session holding a lease cannot wait for another (acquire everything at once instead). Calling it again for a lease you hold returns it and sets holdFor. The person sees the lease on the Resources page and can take it back at any time.
summary: Leases a resource on one of the person's devices (today a Mac's screen through cua-driver) to this session, waiting in a queue when it is busy.
limits: Only resources on devices the session's person owns; not from a session working in an Issue.
compute only on devices where "Allow remote commands from my sessions" is on (the default; the owner can turn it off on the Resources page).
Waits at most 10 minutes per call; a session holding a lease cannot wait for another.
At most 8 resources in one call, all or none.
Kept while the turn runs; afterwards parked at most 10 minutes, or holdFor at most 2 hours; taken 15 minutes after another session starts waiting.
The person can release any lease at any time.

resourceIds.description: Several resources to lease all at once, or none.

type.description: Without resourceId: lease the first ready resource of this type (default computer_use).

deviceId.description: With type: only on this device.

reason.description: What it is for, in a few words; the person sees it in the macOS notification and on the Resources page.

waitMs.description: How long to wait in the queue when it is busy, at most 600000 (10 minutes); 0 (default) answers at once with who holds it.

holdFor.description: Seconds to keep the lease after your turn ends (at most 7200), when the screen must stay as it is until you come back; 0 removes the hold.

name: operate_resource
description: Run one operation, or a short batch in order (stopping at the first failure), on a resource this session leases (acquire_resource). For a Mac's screen the operations are cua-driver's tools: screenshot (returned as an image: a JPEG at most 1280 px on its long edge), get_ui_tree and find_elements (the accessibility tree, with an element_token per element), list_apps, list_windows, open_app, activate_window, click, double_click, right_click, type_text, key, hotkey, scroll, drag, set_value, screen_size and wait. Prefer acting on element_token from get_ui_tree over pixel coordinates; pixel coordinates refer to the window's latest screenshot taken through this lease, so take one first. Input is delivered in the background without moving the person's pointer, except activate_window and drag. screenshotAfter adds a screenshot of the same window after the actions. Each result says ok or an errorCode (stale_lease, lease ended, stale_frame: take a new screenshot; backend_error: what cua-driver said). For a device's compute the operations are run, put_files, get_file, git_sync and cleanup, run by the device's worker as its own user in a scratch folder of Foundry's (scratch names it; the same name finds the same folder in later leases, so a checkout and its installed dependencies stay) or, with workspaceId, in a workspace on that device this session may work in; each result's text is JSON (a run's exitCode, timedOut, durationMs and the tails of stdout and stderr). The lease block of the result says how long you keep it.
summary: Operates a leased resource step by step: screenshots, accessibility tree, clicks, typing, keys, scrolling and dragging on a Mac's screen through cua-driver.
limits: Only with a live lease this session holds; refused once it ended or was taken.
At most 10 actions per call, run in order on the device; at most 120 seconds per call on a screen.

compute: a run blocks at most timeoutSec (default 600, at most 1800) and answers at most 128 KB of each stream's tail; put_files takes 50 MB in pieces of at most 768 KB of base64; get_file answers at most 25 MB per call; nothing outside the scratch folder or the named workspace.
Screenshots at most 1280 px on the long edge and 2 MB each, 8 MB per call; none are kept.
Every operation is audited for the person (typed text as its length only; a command line in full, env as its names, never output).

args.description: The operation's arguments, with cua-driver's own names. Windows are addressed by pid and window_id (from list_windows). screenshot {pid?, window_id?, max_image_dimension? (at most 1280)}: one window (with pid and window_id) or the whole display; get_ui_tree {pid, window_id, query?, max_elements?, max_depth?, include_screenshot?}: the accessibility tree with element_token per element; find_elements {pid, window_id, query}; list_apps {}; list_windows {pid?, on_screen_only?}; open_app {bundle_id | name, urls?}; activate_window {pid, window_id?} (brings it to the front, taking focus); click / double_click / right_click {element_token | x, y, pid?, window_id?, button?, count?, modifier?}; type_text {text, element_token?, pid?, window_id?} (does not press Return); key {key, modifiers?, pid?, window_id?}; hotkey {keys: ["cmd", "c"], pid?, window_id?}; scroll {direction, amount?, by?, element_token? | x, y, pid?, window_id?}; drag {from_x, from_y, to_x, to_y, pid, window_id} (runs in the foreground); set_value {value, element_token?, pid?, window_id?}; screen_size {}; wait {ms} (at most 5000). x and y are pixels in that window's latest screenshot taken through this lease; the backend maps them to the screen. compute (every operation takes scratch? (a folder name, default "default") or workspaceId?; paths are relative to it and cannot leave it): run {argv: ["pnpm", "test"] | command: "shell line", cwd?, env? {NAME: value}, timeoutSec? (default 600, at most 1800), tailBytes? (each stream, default 32768, at most 131072), saveOutput? (a file to write the whole output to)}; put_files {upload (a name you choose), offset (bytes already sent), data (base64 of the next piece), done? (true with the last piece), format? (tar | tar.gz | zip | file; default tar), dest? (folder to unpack into, or for file the file's path)}; get_file {path, offset?, length?}; git_sync {url (https), ref? (branch, tag or commit), dir? (default "repo")}: clones or fetches and checks out ref, keeping ignored files such as node_modules; cleanup {path?}: deletes the scratch folder, or a path in it.

actions.description: Several operations run in order, stopping at the first failure (after op, when both are given).

screenshotAfter.description: Also take a screenshot after the actions (of the window the last action named by pid and window_id, else the whole display).

name: release_resource
description: Release a lease this session holds, as soon as it is done with the resource: the device resets it (keys and buttons up, the backend's session closed) and it goes to the next session waiting. Releasing a lease that already ended answers how it ended.
summary: Releases a lease this session holds so the next session can use the resource.
limits: Only the session holding the lease; the person releases any lease on the Resources page.

name: resource_status
description: Read a resource on one of your person's devices: its state, readiness and backends, who leases it (holder) and how many sessions wait (queue), your own lease on it with when it will be parked or taken (yourLease), and its latest audited operations. Name resourceId, or leaseId for one of your leases.
summary: Shows a resource's state, holder, queue, the session's own lease on it and its latest operations.
limits: Only resources on devices the session's person owns.
The latest 10 operations, as audited (typed text as its length only).

name: list_profiles
description: List the agent profiles you can dispatch to (id, runtime, model, status) on one device: the calling session's device by default, or another device hosting a workspace you reach (see list_workspaces). A profile belongs to its device.
summary: Lists the agent profiles (runtime, model, status) a session can start with on one device.
limits: The calling session's device, or another device hosting a workspace the agent reaches.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: list_models
description: List the models a profile can run (its endpoint's catalog), on your device by default or another device hosting a workspace you reach.
summary: Lists the models a profile can run, from its endpoint's catalog.
limits: The calling session's device, or another device hosting a workspace the agent reaches.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: create_session
description: Create a new Foundry session and deliver it a task. With a session token the new session records you as its parent; in your own workspace (the default) it runs on your device, joins your orchestration group and, without profileId and provider, runs like you. Name workspaceId to start it in another workspace you reach as Member (list_workspaces), on that workspace's device, with your runtime unless you choose a profile there, under that device's model logins (list_resources shows what each device offers). Every session takes a slot on its device, spends model usage and adds a chat to the person's list. Returns the queued session unless wait=true, which blocks until it settles and returns its response. Outside an Issue the new session works in the workspace folder itself, not a copy: sessions writing the same files at once race. A session has at most 8 sessions it started queued, running or blocked at once, and sessions that start sessions nest at most 4 levels below the first one; past either limit create_session is refused. send_message continues an existing session with its context.
summary: Starts a new session with a task, here or in another workspace, and can wait for its answer or start it as a verifier.
limits: At most 8 sessions it started queued, running or blocked at once.
Sessions that start sessions nest at most 4 levels below the first one.
Needs Member in the target workspace; the session runs on that workspace's device, under its logins.
At most 10 attachments, each at most 25 MB, from the caller's own workspace folder.
Waiting lasts at most 10 minutes per call.
A verifier runs in the read-only verification sandbox: the workspace is read-only at the operating-system level, it writes only to its temporary directory, and its Foundry tools only read.

prompt.description: The task brief for the new session.

importedContext.description: Background the new session should know before the prompt.

attachments.description: Files to hand over, as a person's attachments arrive: paths of files in your own workspace folder (absolute, or relative to it), or ids (att_…) of attachments your session was given. Foundry copies each, at most 10 files of up to 25 MB each, into one new folder under .foundry/attachments of the workspace the session runs in, on its device, under their own names, so files sent together can import or include each other. The result's deliveredAttachments and the top of the message list their paths. A session on another device cannot read your workspace: only files handed over here reach it.

verification.description: Start the session as an independent verifier: it runs in the workspace inside a sandbox that keeps the workspace read-only at the operating-system level, for the agent and every command it runs, so tests, linters and git run while anything that would change the workspace fails; it writes only to its own temporary directory outside the workspace, and of the Foundry tools it has only those that read. A device whose worker is older refuses a verifier until its worker is updated.

forkSessionId.description: Fork: a new session that starts from a copy of this session's native transcript, leaving the source untouched. It runs in the source's workspace, on its device, so you need Member there.

issueId.description: Run inside that Issue's candidate worktree and sandbox; the Issue must be in this workspace and in progress, blocked or verifying. A session working in an Issue starts its sessions there without it.

wait.description: Block until the session settles and return its response.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to start the session in, one you reach as Member; defaults to yours with a session token, required without one.

name: handoff_session
description: Start a fresh session that continues another one from facts only: its original goal, last recorded result and status, plus your prompt; never its transcript. Use it instead of forkSessionId when the old transcript is misleading or too long. With a session token the source is a session you control (one your person or their agents started); otherwise any session you can read. The new session starts in workspaceId if given (one you reach as Member), else in the source's workspace; without profileId it runs like the source (its profile on the same device, else its runtime). With a session token it records you as its parent.
summary: Starts a fresh session that continues another from its goal, last result and status plus a new prompt, never its transcript.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started.
Needs Member in the target workspace.

sessionId.description: The session to continue: an id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

prompt.description: What the new session should do next.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to start the new session in; defaults to the source's.

name: list_sessions
description: List the sessions of one workspace, newest activity first, one line each: id, title, status, runtime, profile, device, workspaceId, parentSessionId, activityAt (and issueId, role, source when set). Yours by default; any workspace you reach with workspaceId. parentSessionId lists the sessions one session started (in that session's workspace unless you name another). Pages of limit sessions; pass the nextCursor a page returns as cursor for the next. Read one session's details with read_context.
summary: Lists a workspace's sessions, newest activity first, one line each.
limits: Pages of at most 100 sessions, 30 by default.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

parentOnly.description: Only the sessions your session created (needs a session token).

parentSessionId.description: Only the sessions this session (an id or a Foundry chat link) started.

limit.description: Sessions per page; default 30, at most 100.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.

name: list_group_sessions
description: List the sessions of one orchestration group in list order, in the same one-line form as list_sessions (a device's native chat in the group has kind native_chat). read_context's summary names a session's group. A replacement orchestrator finds a group's sessions here; it controls those its person or their agents started.
summary: Lists the sessions of one orchestration group in list order.
limits: Only groups in workspaces the agent reaches.

workspaceId.description: The group's workspace; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: get_session
description: The same compact summary as read_context with scope=summary, of any session or synced native chat you can read in any workspace you reach: title, status and error, runtime/profile/model, device (and whether it is online), workspace, group, times, lineage, event counts, the last input (first 300 characters) and answer (first 1000), the last error event with the events just before it, and background tasks still open in its latest turn. Read events with read_context scope=events.
summary: Reads one session's or native chat's summary: status, runtime, lineage, last input and answer, last error.
limits: The last input is cut to 300 characters and the answer to 1000.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link (https://<host>/chats/<id>?workspace=…).

name: read_context
description: Read a session or native chat you can read, in any workspace you reach, by id or Foundry link. scope=summary (default) is get_session's summary; events lists its events one line each (time | level | label | detail), filtered by levels, labels and query, newest with tail or paged with after/before cursors, within maxBytes; thread (the session's full transcript), transcript (raw native chat) and subagents (the session's native subagents; with taskId, one subagent's transcript) return JSON cut at maxBytes. What a session produced: changes lists the files its own tools wrote and its answers named, one line each with the lines added and removed (with path: that file's diff, the whole session's or one turn's with inputId); file with path reads one of those files as it is now on the session's device; background lists the commands it left running in the background (with taskId: the end of one's output, which needs Member in the session's workspace). A thread or transcript can run to megabytes.
summary: Reads a session in depth: its events, transcript, native subagents, the files it changed and the commands it left running.
limits: Output is cut at maxBytes, 12000 by default.
Pages of at most 500 events, with up to 5 events of context each.
A background command's output needs Member in the session's workspace.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link (https://<host>/chats/<id>?workspace=…).

levels.description: scope=events: only events of these levels, e.g. ["error","warning"].

labels.description: scope=events: only events with these labels (exact, case-insensitive), e.g. ["Session failed"].

query.description: scope=events: only events whose label, detail or message contains this text (case-insensitive).

tail.description: scope=events: the last N matching events (at most 500). Without it, the first `limit` matches.

limit.description: scope=events: page size without tail; default 50, at most 500.

after.description: scope=events: only events after this cursor, an event id this tool printed or a time (2026-10-09T20:40:00Z).

before.description: scope=events: only events before this cursor, an event id or a time.

context.description: scope=events: also show up to N events (at most 5) just before each match, to see what led to it.

taskId.description: With scope=subagents: the subagent to read. With scope=background: the task whose output to read.

path.description: With scope=changes: the file whose diff to read; with scope=file: the file to read. A path changes lists.

inputId.description: With scope=changes and path: only what that turn (an input id changes lists) changed.

maxBytes.description: Default 12000. events keeps whole lines within it and prints the cursor that continues; background output keeps its end.

name: list_issues
description: List the Issues of one workspace, most recently updated first, one line each: id, shortId, title, status, contract (its state and confirmed revision), run (the status of its latest execution), question (the kind of question waiting for the person, if any) and verified (required criteria passed of total). Yours by default; any workspace you reach with workspaceId. A session working in an Issue sees only that Issue. Read one with get_issue. Issues are read-only here: the person drives them in Foundry.
summary: Lists a workspace's Issues with their status, contract, latest run and verification progress.
limits: Read-only: the person drives Issues in Foundry.
A session working in an Issue sees only that Issue.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: get_issue
description: Read one Issue you can reach: status (and why it is blocked), the person's request, the confirmed contract (revision, goal, scope, constraints and each criterion with its latest verification verdict) and whether a newer draft waits for confirmation, the question waiting for the person, the verification summary and whether the latest review allows acceptance, and its latest execution run (its session id, which read_context reads, status and error).
summary: Reads one Issue: the request, the confirmed contract with each criterion's verdict, the waiting question and the latest run.
limits: Read-only: the person drives Issues in Foundry.
A session working in an Issue sees only that Issue.

issueId.description: The Issue's id (iss_…) or short id.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to a session you control: one your person or their agents started, in a workspace you reach as Member (a session working in an Issue: only that Issue's sessions), except an Issue's own execution or clarification, which their Issue drives. A running session is steered (Claude adjusts its active turn; Codex queues it for the next one). An idle session takes it as its next input and continues the same native session; profileId/provider/model switch its runtime first (only while it is idle). wait=true blocks until it settles and returns its response.
summary: Messages a session: steers a running one or continues an idle one, and can switch its runtime first.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started, in workspaces reached as Member; in an Issue, only the Issue's sessions.
Never an Issue's execution or clarification: their Issue drives them.
The runtime switches only while the session is idle.
At most 10 attachments, each at most 25 MB, from the caller's own workspace folder.
Waiting lasts at most 10 minutes per call.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

attachments.description: Files to hand over, as a person's attachments arrive: paths of files in your own workspace folder (absolute, or relative to it), or ids (att_…) of attachments your session was given. Foundry copies each, at most 10 files of up to 25 MB each, into one new folder under .foundry/attachments of the workspace the session runs in, on its device, under their own names, so files sent together can import or include each other. The result's deliveredAttachments and the top of the message list their paths. A session on another device cannot read your workspace: only files handed over here reach it.

wait.description: Block until the session settles and return its response.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

name: cancel_session
description: Stop the work a session you control is doing (one your person or their agents started, in a workspace you reach as Member; a session working in an Issue: only that Issue's sessions). Cancelling never cascades: sessions it created keep running. The session stays usable: send_message continues it.
summary: Stops the work a session is doing; the session stays usable.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started, in workspaces reached as Member; in an Issue, only the Issue's sessions.
Never cascades: the sessions it started keep running.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: wait_session
description: Block until a session you can read reaches one of the requested statuses (default: completed/failed/canceled) or the timeout elapses, and return it with its response once settled.
summary: Waits until a session reaches the given statuses and returns its answer once it settles.
limits: Waits at most 10 minutes per call.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

until.description: Statuses to wait for, e.g. ["running"]; default completed, failed and canceled.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, at most 600000 (10 minutes, the default). If the session is still running when it elapses, call wait_session again.

name: rename_session
description: Rename a session you control (1-120 characters): one your person or their agents started, in a workspace you reach as Member (a session working in an Issue: only that Issue's sessions).
summary: Renames a session.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started, in workspaces reached as Member; in an Issue, only the Issue's sessions.
Titles of 1–120 characters.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: ask_person
description: Ask the person something only they can decide (a choice the confirmed contract leaves open) or allow (a side effect outside the candidate, such as deploying or sending a message). Only an Issue's execution has this tool. After calling it, end your turn with a short summary of where you are; the Issue waits for the person and Foundry resumes you in the same candidate with their answer. Ask one question at a time and never about anything you can decide yourself.
summary: Asks the person what only they can decide or allow; the Issue waits for the answer and Foundry resumes the session with it.
limits: Only an Issue's execution has it.
Questions of up to 4000 bytes, with up to 6 suggested answers.

question.description: What you need, in the person's language, with the context they need to answer.

kind.description: input: a decision or information; permission: approval for a specific action. Defaults to input.

options.description: Up to 6 suggested answers; the person may answer otherwise.

name: feishu_events
description: Receive Feishu events (messages, card actions, approvals: whatever the app subscribes to in the Feishu console) of a Feishu app your person connected in Connectors. Call it without subscriptionId to subscribe: it returns a subscriptionId and buffers matching events from then on. Call it again with that subscriptionId to get what arrived since the last call, waiting up to timeoutMs for the first event; events come in order with a cursor each, and the full Feishu payload. Calling again acknowledges what the last call returned; to read an answer you lost, pass the cursor it started from. Unsubscribe when done. You may reply as the bot with feishu-cli; `feishu-cli event consume` receives the same events.
summary: Subscribes to a connected Feishu app's events and returns them by cursor, waiting for the next.
limits: Only apps the session's person connected in Connectors.
At most 8 subscriptions per session, each buffering at most 500 unread events; beyond that the oldest are dropped and counted.
At most 100 events per call; waits at most 10 minutes per call.
A subscription nobody calls for 30 minutes ends.

subscriptionId.description: The subscription to read (fsub_…); omit to subscribe.

appId.description: When subscribing: the Feishu app id (cli_…) or the Connectors app id (xapp_…). Optional if your person connected exactly one Feishu app.

eventTypes.description: When subscribing: event types to keep, e.g. ["im.message.receive_v1"]; default every type.

chatId.description: When subscribing: keep only events in this chat (oc_…).

cursor.description: Return events after this cursor; default after the last call's answer.

maxEvents.description: At most this many events, up to 100 (default 50). more: true says others are waiting.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the first event, at most 600000 (10 minutes); default 0 when subscribing and 60000 when reading. 0 answers at once.

unsubscribe.description: End the subscription named by subscriptionId.
